name: Matthew R. Walter
title: Associate Professor
department: Computer Science; Robot Intelligence through Perception Laboratory
fitReason: Excellent overlap with embodied AI, 3D perception, natural-language grounding and physically grounded human-AI collaboration. Recent work connects haptic demonstration quality to learned manipulation policies and camera geometry to policy generalization.

physicalEvidence.summary: The March 31, 2026 HapCompass primary paper details a physical robot arm with tactile three-finger gripper, wrist force-torque sensor and hand-tracking teleoperation. Experiments include physical key/USB insertion and fragile probing, plus imitation-policy rollouts from collected demonstrations. A separate 2026 project description documents UR5 camera-conditioned manipulation.

shortVisit.summary: RIPL explicitly encourages applications to TTIC's Visiting Student/Intern Program. The live program accepts current graduate students and international applicants; offers are initiated by listed faculty hosts. Typical summer duration is 12–15 weeks (about three months), so an approximately eight-week visit needs explicit approval. Apply roughly 5–6 months before desired start. Funding varies; the institution acknowledges occasional volunteer visits. No summer 2027 host commitment or funding amount is confirmed.

unknowns: Eight weeks is shorter than TTIC's stated usual 12–15-week summer visit. Do not present the standard program as duration-compatible without approval.
International English evidence is required before an offer; currently listed options include AEPA, TOEFL speaking and IELTS Academic speaking thresholds. Recheck for 2027.
Health insurance and University of Chicago student-life privileges are required, with fees. Travel and relocation are typically not covered; exact support depends on the host and funding.
The Institute's mention of volunteer visits does not establish a particular visitor’s appointment or visa eligibility. Self-funding must be approved through the formal program.
Current official faculty directory and personal page say Associate Professor; general news uses Professor as a broad address.
